project.name: Jam
project.description: Your sats. Your privacy. Your profit.

releases.name: v2.0.0-beta.1
releases.body_excerpt:
_"The flower that blooms in adversity is the most rare and beautiful of all"_ Second beta of Jam Version `v2.0.0` is out! 

This is the second release compatible with the new [`joinmarket-ng`](https://github.com/joinmarket-ng/joinmarket-ng) backend.
Support for [`joinmarket-clientserver`](https://github.com/JoinMarket-Org/joinmarket-clientserver) has been removed.

---

⚠️ **Jam is considered beta software.** ⚠️  

The new backend `joinamarket-ng` is bleeding edge and things might break
releases.author: theborakompanioni

releases.name: v2.0.0-beta.0
releases.body_excerpt:
_"The very things that hold you down are going to lift you up."_ First beta of Jam Version `v2.0.0` is out! 

This is the first release compatible with the new [`joinmarket-ng`](https://github.com/joinmarket-ng/joinmarket-ng) backend.
[`joinmarket-clientserver`](https://github.com/JoinMarket-Org/joinmarket-clientserver) was archived on Apr 27, 2026. While this release should still work with `joinmarket-clientserver` backends, support will be dropped soon and usage is discouraged.

---

⚠️
releases.author: theborakompanioni

releases.name: v0.4.1 - Happy Honeydew
releases.body_excerpt:
_"The past can hurt. But the way I see it, you can either run from it or learn from it.."_ Jam Version `v0.4.1` is out! 

---

Here's what's fixed:
- Fix total balance after tx (#947)

Refer to the individual PRs and the changelog below for details.

---

⚠️ **Jam is _still_ considered beta software.** ⚠️  

While JoinMarket is tried and tested, Jam is new and things might break. Use with caution.

Please report any issues [directly on GitHub](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/j
releases.author: theborakompanioni

releases.name: v0.4.0 - Glossy Guava
releases.body_excerpt: _"All you need is faith, trust, and a little bit of pixie dust."_ Jam Version `v0.4.0` is out! releases.name: v0.3.0 - Freezing Fig
releases.body_excerpt:
_"I Don't Care What They're Going To Say, Let The Storm Rage On, The Cold Never Bothered Me Anyway!"_ Jam Version `v0.3.0` is out! This release adds an easy way to [quickly freeze/unfreeze UTXOs](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/jam/issues/771), [review eligible or selected UTXOs](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/jam/issues/773) before sending, and fixes a couple of other things. 

---

Here's what's new:
- Quickly freeze/unfreeze UTXOs on send page (#771)
- Review eligible or select

releases.body_excerpt:

releases.name: v0.1.5 - Blueberry Bonus
releases.body_excerpt: Jam [Version `0.1.5`](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/jam/milestone/11?closed=1) is out! These blue berries run on [JoinMarket v0.9.9](https://github.com/JoinMarket-Org/joinmarket-clientserver/releases/tag/v0.9.9), the latest and greatest of all the JoinMarkets. You can read all about the various bugfixes and improvements that happened under the hood in the [JoinMarket v0.9.9 release notes](https://github.com/JoinMarket-Org/joinmarket-clientserver/blob/master/docs/release-notes/release-notes

releases.name: v0.1.4 - Pineberry Performance
releases.body_excerpt:
Elf on a shelf? Jam on a lamb? Months come in twelves, and Jam [Version `0.1.4`](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/jam/milestone/14?closed=1) just hit the shelves!

---

- You can now unlock your [fidelity bonds](https://jamdocs.org/market/fees/) again (once they are expired) (#556)
- The settings page is now a bit more orderly, thanks to subsections added by @benalleng (#573)

releases.name: v0.1.3 - Durian Delay
releases.body_excerpt:
It's a stinky fruit, but (hopefully) not a stinky release! [Version `0.1.3`](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/jam/milestone/15?closed=1). Nothing earth shattering, just some minor improvements, including one that should hopefully fix a startup delay bug we had.

---

Here's what's new:
- You can now quickly adjust your [fee settings](https://jamdocs.org/market/fees/) before doing a sweep (#565)
- We also made the orderbook a bit easier on the eyes (#563)

releases.name: v0.1.2 - Fresh Figs
releases.body_excerpt:
Figs?! Yes, bugfigs! This is another bugfix release. [Version `0.1.2`](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/jam/milestone/13?closed=1).

---

Here's what's new:
- Nothing.

Here's what's fixed:
- Display an actual error message if the backend is unreachable (#540)
- Don't show the nitty-gritty development thingies for manual installs (#549)
- Minor cosmetical issues.

releases.name: v0.1.1 - Feisty Fees
releases.body_excerpt:
The god-damn fees are too damn high! 21 days later, and we're patching it up! ---

releases.name: v0.1.0 - Tasty Parity
releases.body_excerpt:
Is this real life? The first minor release, [version `0.1.0`](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/joinmarket-webui/milestone/7?closed=1) of Jam is out the door! Wohoo! 🎉

- Highlight your offers in the in-app [Orderbook](https://jamdo

releases.body_excerpt:
Oh my Lord! [Version `0.0.10`](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/joinmarket-webui/milestone/10?closed=1) of Jam is out!

releases.body_excerpt:

releases.body_excerpt:

- 🫙 Jars, jars, jars. Improvements around jars. Did I mention jars? #344, #345, #346

releases.name: v0.0.5 - Sweep Sweep Jam
releases.body_excerpt:
Sweet! [Version 0.0.5](https://github.com/joinmarket-webui/joinmarket-webui/milestone/2?closed=1) of Jam is out! 🍯 

Here is the gist:
* Sweep functionality #184 
* TypeScript support #176 
* i18n support for all screen #174 
* Seed quiz #156 

The goal of this project is to bring [JoinMarket](https://github.com/JoinMarket-Org/joinmarket-clientserver) to a wider audience by providing an interface that is—hopefully—both appealing and easy to use.

releases.name: v0.0.4 - Bugfixes & Cleanup
releases.body_excerpt:
Version 0.0.4 of Jam is out! 🚀 This version adds basic i18n support and fixes some minor issues. 

The goal of this project is to bring [JoinMarket](https://github.com/JoinMarket-Org/joinmarket-clientserver) to a wider audience by providing an interface that is—hopefully—both appealing and easy to use.
